messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a new regression on H100 when running long-context workloads with paged KV. Memory growth shows repeated page churn and page table entry flips (not just evictions).
ajay: Can you paste the profiler traces? Is this correlated with the tiled kernel switch from last week?
maria: Quick log excerpt: 
```
KV: alloc page 0x3f2a, mapped -> slot 42
KV: evict page 0x3f2a -> writeback
KV: remap page 0x3f2a -> slot 17
KV: pageflip: pte owner changed unexpectedly
```
Observed ~10-20x higher amortized page remaps at ~32k token sequences. Happens only on H100 + latest kernel selection path. MI250x looks stable.
dave: Interesting. On H100 we changed kernel selection to prefer tiled-attn for sequences >8k. That also changes prefetch/alloc patterns in the pager. Could be a race in remap path.
maria: Repro command: `python tools/repro_kvcache.py --model=redwood-14b --seq=32768 --gpu=h100 --runs=50` — run for ~5 mins and you'll see pageflip spikes in `kv-pager.log`.
ajay: I ran the repro, attached perf-bot output: 
perf-bot: [summary] 50 runs H100: page remap events per run median=1423, 95p=3120; longctx allocation growth +18% after 10min; kernel switch events coincide with remap spikes.
maria: Also saw fragmentation: many small free slots and reuse window misses. Eviction rate stays steady but reuse drops. Suggests page table metadata gets transiently inconsistent, forcing reclaim instead of reuse.
dave: Can you capture `nvprof` or CUPTI timeline around a remap spike? Need to see whether CUDA stream ordering differs between tiled kernels and baseline.
maria: Will capture tonight. Logged a short stacktrace where remap path asserts: `pt->owner != NULL but owner != expected`.
ajay: Could be stale owner pointer from async evict completion callback. We also changed batching heuristics (coalesced batches) — that increases parallel evict completions.
dave: Reassigning to ajay + maria. I'll add a small fence in the evict completion handler to see if it masks the problem. If it does, it's ordering. If not, deeper metadata race.
maria: FYI, MI250x trace didn't show owner flip, but we did see more hot page reuse there. GPU allocator behavior differs (H100 uses different page alignment for tiled kernels).
ajay: I'll instrument the page table writes with seq IDs and log both before/after remap. Also will add a metric for reuse-window misses.
maria: Thanks. If anyone else sees similar on other H100 clusters, please ping.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/evict-fence-test -> eng-runtime/staging at 2024-09-18T02:05:00Z :eyes:
ajay: pushed a small test patch that adds ordering fence in evict completion; running canary now. Results expected in ~30m.
maria: Appreciated. If canary masks it we'll iterate on lightweight sync or move to atomic owner swaps.
perf-bot: [canary] patch/evict-fence-test on h100-canary-2: 30 runs median page remap=98 (was 1423), reuse-window miss rate down 88% — preliminary positive.
dave: Great signal. Let's keep this in staging while we root-cause. If fencing fixes it, we still need a proper fix (less perf impact) — maybe switch to compare-and-swap owner updates.
maria: Agreed. I opened an issue with logs + nvprof when done: https://stash.local/r/ENGRUNTIME/issues/3245 (will attach traces).
ajay: I'll follow up with a micro-benchmark to confirm perf delta of the fence vs CAS.
maria: Updating the thread as I collect timelines. TL;DR: H100 tiled-kernel + new batching heuristics exposed an eviction completion ordering bug that flips PTE owners; fence masks it, CAS likely ultimate fix.
